name: copy_word_rows_long_offset
description: Copies rows of 16-bit words from a source pointer to a destination pointer, moving the destination on by an offset built from a register and a constant between passes. The row length and pass count arrive in registers, and the loops run over fixed pass counts.

name: copy_word_rows_short_offset
description: Performs the same nested word-row copy as its neighbour, with a smaller constant in the destination offset. Its loop counts and register inputs are otherwise identical.

name: clear_three_blocks_then_copy
description: Zeroes three blocks of 720 longwords spaced 8000 bytes apart, then stores an input register value plus four in a state record field and calls the word-row copy routine. It finishes by writing fourteen words from the source into the second word of each four-byte table entry.

name: copy_rows_around_pointer_store
description: Calls the word-row copy routine, stores the address left in a register plus twelve into a state record field, and calls the word-row copy routine again. It has no other effects.

name: clear_longword_block_fixed
description: Writes zero to 2880 consecutive longwords starting at a fixed memory address. It calls nothing and reads no registers.

name: or_four_planes_into_frame
description: Runs up to 72 frames, copying rows on each frame and then ORing four equally spaced longword sources, ten longwords per row, into a destination buffer. It stops early when a flag byte in the state record is set.

name: copy_longwords_to_four_planes
description: Copies ten longwords from a source block to a destination and, in the same pass, copies three further source blocks to destinations spaced 8000 bytes apart. Each row is therefore written to four destinations.

name: poll_routine_until_flag
description: Runs up to sixteen passes, calling an unnamed routine once per pass and then sixteen times calling a second unnamed routine and storing each return value in one fixed word. It stops early when a flag byte in the state record becomes nonzero.

name: set_stop_flag_when_enabled
description: Calls two unnamed routines, then sets a stop byte in the state record to all ones when another byte in the record is nonzero.

name: step_mismatched_nibble_fields
description: Fills sixteen table words with a value whose three 4-bit fields are all at maximum, then runs sixteen rows. Each row calls two unnamed routines and, for every entry, steps each 4-bit field that differs from the source word down by one.

name: run_tagged_hook_until_change
description: Repeatedly calls through a pointer held in a global while that global holds the four-character tag 'MON:', looping until a word in the state record becomes nonzero and differs from its starting value. It then clears that word and calls two unnamed routines.

name: repeat_call_countdown_loop
description: Calls an unnamed routine once per step while counting a 16-bit register down from its entry value until it passes below zero.

name: toggle_mode_on_trigger
description: When a trigger byte in the state record equals a fixed marker value, it clears the trigger and flips a mode byte between zero and all ones. Each branch calls unnamed routines and writes a few globals to match the new mode.

name: store_three_registers
description: Writes the values of three data registers into three consecutive global longwords. It does nothing else and calls nothing.

name: stub_unrecovered_single_instruction
description: The decompiler timed out, so only the facts are known: one instruction, called from two unnamed routines, with no recorded calls or hardware access. It is recorded as a stub because no behaviour can be named from the evidence.

name: return_input_unchanged
description: Returns the value passed in one data register unchanged, so it acts as a pass-through. The listed hardware register reference does not appear in the pseudo-code, which only returns that value.

name: decode_xor_stream_to_buffer
description: Enables DMA and interrupts, zeroes a 10240-longword buffer, and XOR-decodes a marker-terminated byte stream into it, with marker values for end-of-run, end-of-stream and a two-byte offset form. It then reads sixteen rows of 32 words through an unnamed routine and disables DMA and interrupts again.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The decompiler shows only a halt on bad instruction data, so no behaviour is recovered and the routine is a stub. Its single recorded caller is a tiny routine.

name: stub_immediate_return
description: Does nothing and returns at once. The pseudo-code has no calls, register writes or memory access.

name: decrement_nonzero_nibble_fields
description: Takes a 12-bit word and steps each of its three 4-bit fields down by one when that field is nonzero. It returns the recombined word.

name: wait_for_marker_byte_twice
description: Spins twice in succession until a byte in the state record equals a fixed quote-mark character, then returns. It touches no hardware.

name: store_five_pointer_pairs
description: Stores five pointer values into consecutive global longword pairs, each followed by a count of five. It calls nothing and does nothing else.

name: poll_interrupt_request_counter
description: Tests one bit of the interrupt request register and, when it is set, sets a global to a fixed value and decrements a 16-bit counter if it is nonzero. It writes no hardware registers.

name: initialise_audio_channel_state
description: When a flag byte in the state record is clear, builds running-sum tables from a source table, zeroes the four audio channel volume registers and sets a global to a sentinel value.

name: silence_audio_channels
description: Clears a global counter and the four audio channel volume registers, then writes a DMA control value that disables the DMA bits of the four audio channels.

name: process_audio_channel_commands
description: Runs only while a global tick counter is nonzero, decrementing it and interpreting a per-channel command record for each of four audio channels. Commands update period, volume, sample pointer and sample length registers, which are then written for each channel.

name: clamp_level_enter_update_loop
description: Clamps a level byte to the smaller of its value and a global limit, stores it in a channel record, and enters the shared update loop. That loop clamps each output word to the global limit and writes it out.

name: store_word_enter_update_loop
description: Stores its word argument in a channel record field and enters the shared update loop, which clamps each output word to a global limit and writes it out.

name: store_lookup_byte_enter_loop
description: Stores its word argument in a channel record and copies a byte from a global table into another field, then enters the shared update loop. That loop clamps each output word to a global limit and writes it out.

name: store_flag_byte_enter_loop
description: Stores a byte argument in a channel record field and enters the shared update loop, which clamps each output word to a global limit and writes it out.

name: run_shared_update_loop
description: Enters the shared update loop directly, clamping each output word to a global limit and writing it out. It is called from three unnamed routines and calls one unnamed routine.

name: dispatch_channel_commands
description: Lowers a level field by a step, clamped to a minimum, then reads command bytes and calls the matching handler from a jump table for each one in range. It stops at a zero or out-of-range command byte.

name: step_level_toward_target
description: Moves a level field toward a target by a step amount, snapping to the target when it is reached. When called with a mode code of sixteen, it also updates and clamps an accumulator byte and calls two unnamed routines.

name: stub_immediate_return
description: Returns immediately with no body, and two unnamed routines take its address. Nothing is done, so it is recorded as a stub.

name: run_frame_state_machine
description: Repeatedly calls an unnamed routine while a counter field stays unchanged, then checks two state bytes to choose between restarting a sequence and advancing a counter that wraps from twelve back to one. It also tests a global against a fixed tag before calling through a pointer held in a global.

name: dispatch_by_state_index
description: Calls the routine selected from a table by a 16-bit index stored in the state record, scaling the index to four-byte table entries. It has no other effects.

name: initialise_timing_defaults
description: Calls several unnamed routines around a fixed longword constant that is stored in one record field and copied into a second, and clears two globals. It ends with one more call.

name: initialise_state_record_defaults
description: Calls three unnamed routines, stores two fixed pointer constants and several starting values into the state record, then calls one more routine.

name: initialise_sequence_record_fields
description: Clears a block of 122 words, copies a setup record chosen by an index into the state record, and derives three pointers from fixed base values offset by multiples of 48 bytes. It also sets timing and frame fields to starting values and calls several unnamed routines.

name: call_routine_sequence_in_order
description: Calls a fixed sequence of unnamed routines in order, with no data handling of its own.

name: call_three_routines_in_order
description: Calls three unnamed routines in sequence and returns. It handles no data of its own.

name: copy_longwords_from_header_length
description: Copies a block of longwords from a source to a destination, with the count read from a packed length field stored four bytes before the source. The count is shifted, masked and reduced by one before the loop runs.

name: copy_longwords_by_register_count
description: Copies longwords from a source to a destination using a count taken from a data register, divided by four and reduced by one. It is the same copy loop as the previous routine, with the count supplied in a register.

name: advance_step_on_table_match
description: While a stop flag is clear, calls an unnamed routine and compares a state byte with an entry in a byte table indexed by a step counter. A match advances the counter and marks the byte, a mismatch resets the counter, and reaching the final step clears two globals and sets the stop flag.

name: fill_table_rows_with_markers
description: Fills a table of 48 rows, each starting with an all-ones word followed by a run of zero words.

name: start_copper_and_interrupts
description: The decompiler timed out, so only facts are known: it touches the copper list pointer, the copper jump strobe, the DMA control register, the interrupt enable register and a parallel port status register. It calls six routines, one of them a tiny constant-loading routine.

name: build_pointer_table_from_index
description: Builds six pointer halves that step by the input value, writes a decimal digit derived from the input into a text location, copies sixteen words from a table selected by the input, and sets fixed words in the state record. It calls two unnamed routines.

name: store_word_then_call_routine
description: Stores a fixed word into a global location and calls an unnamed routine, then writes a word with the top bit clear and all other bits set to a register at a fixed offset from the base pointer.

name: wait_for_global_marker_byte
description: Spins until a global byte equals a period character, then returns. The facts also record a read of the video beam position register, which the shown pseudo-code does not contain.

name: set_flag_or_spin_forever
description: If a bit in a global is already set, it spins forever; otherwise it sets that bit and returns. The facts also record timer and keyboard serial register touches that the pseudo-code does not contain.

name: store_three_registers
description: Writes the values of three data registers into three consecutive global longwords. It does nothing else and calls nothing.

name: stub_unrecovered_single_instruction
description: The decompiler timed out, so only facts are known: a single instruction, called from a tiny routine and one unnamed routine. No calls or hardware access are recorded, so it is a stub.

name: stub_immediate_return
description: Returns immediately with no body and no calls. Only a tiny routine calls it.

name: stub_immediate_return
description: Returns immediately with no body and no calls. It is reached only in the reference run, and its body is a bare return.

name: stub_immediate_return
description: Returns immediately with no body and no calls. It is reached only in the reference run, and its body is a bare return.

name: stub_immediate_return
description: Returns immediately with no body and no calls. It is reached only in the reference run, and its body is a bare return.

name: stub_immediate_return
description: Returns immediately with no body and no calls. It is reached only in the reference run, and its body is a bare return.

name: stub_immediate_return
description: Returns immediately with no body and no calls. It is reached only in the reference run, and its body is a bare return.

name: stub_raw_region_entry
description: The decompiler timed out, so only facts are known: one instruction at the start of a raw code region in the alien data file. No calls, callers or hardware registers are recorded.

name: configure_copper_and_interrupts
description: The decompiler timed out, so only facts are known: a 73-instruction routine at the start of a raw intro code region that touches the copper list pointer, DMA control, interrupt enable and interrupt request registers. It makes three unnamed calls.

name: test_interrupt_request_register
description: The decompiler timed out, so only facts are known: a 45-instruction routine that touches the interrupt request register and its read copy and makes one unnamed call. It is called from a tiny routine.

name: configure_audio_channel_zero
description: The decompiler timed out, so only facts are known: a 53-instruction routine that touches audio channel zero's pointer, length, period and volume registers, the audio-disk control register, the DMA control register and the interrupt request register. It is called from a tiny routine.

name: stub_unrecovered_small_routine
description: The decompiler timed out, so only facts are known: a 17-instruction routine with one unnamed call and a tiny-routine caller. It is recorded as a stub because no behaviour can be named.

name: stub_unrecovered_routine_entry
description: The decompiler timed out, so only facts are known: a 30-instruction routine called by two unnamed routines, with no recorded calls or hardware access. It is recorded as a stub because no behaviour can be named.
